transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... well, I guess what made me come in is that for the past year or so, I've been having a little trouble staying on track. It's probably not a huge deal—I mean, I know everyone gets sidetracked sometimes, right? But it just seems like the smallest thing kind of pulls me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. 

Like, it could just be my phone buzzing, or somebody walking past my office door. Or even just a random thought popping into my head out of nowhere, like something about my in-laws, and suddenly I'm completely off task. 

I hope that doesn't sound too silly? I just want to make sure I'm doing my best at work and not letting things slip, you know? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Are these difficulties with staying on track causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say a *lot* of stress! I mean, I’m still keeping up overall. I don't want you to think I'm completely dropping the ball or anything like that. I manage to get things done. 

But... well, I guess it is causing a little bit of friction? I’m just noticing that it’s starting to cost me some trust at home, maybe. And... I think I'm losing some patience from people at work, too. Like, when I'm running meetings, or having mentoring conversations with my team, or even just trying to stick to family plans on the weekend... sometimes things just don’t go the way they should because my mind is bouncing around. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I just want to make sure I'm doing right by everyone, you know? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse or doing things without fully thinking them through?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, running a company, I kind of have to be pretty careful about my decisions, right? So I try really hard to think things through as best as I can. I wouldn't say I'm impulsive... at least, I really hope I don't come across that way. 

I mean, sometimes you have to make quick calls in business, but I always try to weigh the options first so I don't let anyone down. I haven't really noticed myself just doing things without thinking. Is it okay if that's not really an issue for me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, sitting still for a long time is tough for anyone, right? 

But, um, I do notice that in meetings, I'm usually, you know, bouncing my knee under the table, or maybe clicking a pen. Just little things! I try to keep it quiet. Or I'll find myself shifting around in my chair a lot. 

It's just extra energy, really, but... well, I've noticed people have started giving me these looks. Like they think I'm trying to rush them along, or that I'm not paying attention. And I *am* trying to listen, I really am! I'd hate for my team to think I don't value what they're saying. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too antsy or disrespectful. I just like to keep moving, I guess. Is that normal for someone in my position?
Do you find it hard to finish tasks or projects because you lose focus or get distracted?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I *can't* finish things. I definitely get things done! I mean, I have to, right? 

But, I guess... well, maybe I do struggle a little bit with keeping my focus the whole time. Like, I can sit down to start a planning document, or I'll be in a one-on-one with one of my managers, and for the first few minutes, I am completely locked in. I'm right there with them. 

But then... I don't know, pretty soon I'll realize I kind of drifted off? And I end up having to ask them to run it back because I missed half of what they said. I always feel so bad when I have to do that. I try to play it off like I just want to make sure I'm fully understanding their point, because I really don't want them to think I don't care about their work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible boss. I just... my mind wanders sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you're having trouble staying on track or finishing tasks?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I really try not to let things get to me like that. 

I mean, if I'm having a little trouble staying on a task, I usually just... well, I just pivot to something else for a bit, you know? I don't really sit there and feel anxious or overwhelmed. I think, especially being the one in charge, you kind of have to keep a level head, right? If I look stressed out, then my team might start worrying, and I definitely don't want to put that on them. 

So, no, I don't think I get anxious about it. I just try to roll with it and get back on track when I can. Is that... I mean, I hope that's a good thing? I just try to handle it the best way I can so I'm not a burden on anyone else.
Are your difficulties with staying on track and getting distracted causing problems in your relationships with your family or team members?

Well, um... I really hope it's not causing major problems. I mean, I'm still keeping up with everything overall! I make sure the important stuff gets done. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it might be causing a little bit of friction? Just minor things. Like, at home, my wife gets a bit frustrated when we have plans and I kind of... lose track of time or get sidetracked. I think she feels like she can't always rely on me to follow through exactly how we talked about, which I feel terrible about. I really want to be dependable for her.

And at work... well, like I mentioned with the meetings and mentoring my managers, I think I'm starting to test their patience a little. When a conversation doesn't go the way it should because I lost the thread, I can tell they get a little exasperated, even if they're too polite to say it. 

I'm trying really hard to manage it, though! I just... I want everyone to feel supported and heard, and I hate thinking I'm letting them down. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound like everything is falling apart, because it really isn't. Just... a few bumps in the road, I guess?
Are there any areas of your life where you feel like you're not performing as well as you used to due to these distractions?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say my performance has dropped or anything like that. I'm definitely still hitting my goals and keeping the company moving forward. I mean, you kind of have to when you're the CEO, right? You can't just let things slide. 

I guess... well, maybe it just takes me a little more effort to get the same results sometimes? Like, I might have to work a little later or put in some extra hours on the weekend to make sure everything is tied up neatly, but I always get it done. I wouldn't say I'm underperforming at all. 

I really try to make sure I'm giving my best everywhere—at work and at home. I mean, I hope that's what it looks like from the outside, anyway. Do you think it's normal to just have to work a little harder to keep up sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm doing things right.
Do you often feel like you're constantly 'on the go' or like you're driven by a motor?

Well, um... I suppose I do have a lot of energy. I try to channel it into my work, mostly! But... yeah, if I'm in a spot where I'm really supposed to just sit quietly... like during family dinners, or, um, my church volunteer meetings... I do kind of feel that way. 

It's like there's this little motor running inside me. I don't want to be disruptive, obviously, so I usually just try to, you know, move a little bit or find something to do with my hands. Like fiddling with a pen or a napkin, just to keep that energy managed so I'm not bothering anyone else. 

It's not a huge deal or anything, I just... I guess I'm just used to being productive. That's pretty normal for someone who runs a company, right? You just get used to always being "on." I really try to keep it under wraps, though. I just hope it doesn't come across as rude to my family or the church folks... do you think that sounds okay?
Are you finding it harder to maintain your current level of responsibility at work or at home due to your difficulties with staying on track?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm dropping the ball or anything like that. I'm definitely still keeping up with all my responsibilities overall! I always make sure the important things get handled. 

But... I guess, to be completely honest... maybe it is getting a little harder to keep everyone, you know, happy? Like I was mentioning before, I worry it's starting to cost me a little bit of trust at home when our family plans don't go the way they should. And at work... I really hate to admit it, but I think I'm losing some of the patience from my team when those meetings or mentoring conversations go off track. 

I'm still doing my job, I promise! I just... I really want to be a good leader and a good husband, and it bothers me to think I might be frustrating them. It's just a little stressful trying to make sure I don't let anyone down. That makes sense, right? Do you think it's pretty normal to have these kinds of growing pains when you're trying to manage so much?
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities at work or at home because of your difficulties with staying on track?

Well, um... I know we just kind of touched on this, and I really want to be clear that I'm not failing at my job or anything. I'm definitely still keeping up with everything overall. I make sure the bills are paid, the company is running, all of that. 

But, I mean... since you're asking again... I guess it is starting to take a little bit of a toll in other ways. Like I said, I'm just starting to worry that it's costing me some trust at home. You know, when family plans get derailed because I got sidetracked. And at work... I can kind of tell I'm losing some patience from my team when those meetings or the mentoring stuff I do just... doesn't go the way it should because I lost focus. 

I'm really trying my best to keep everyone happy, though! I just... I don't want to be a disappointment to them. That's a normal thing to worry about, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for the people who count on me.
Do you have difficulty managing your emotions, such as feeling overly angry or irritable?

Oh, um, no... I wouldn't say that at all. I actually try really hard to be a positive guy. I mean, sure, running a business can be stressful sometimes, but I don't really get angry or, you know, snap at people. I always try to keep my cool. 

You kind of have to be level-headed if you want your team to respect you, right? And I'd never want to take anything out on my wife, either. So, no, I don't really struggle with irritability or anything like that. I like to think I'm pretty easy to get along with... I hope that's a good sign?
Are your difficulties with staying on track significantly interfering with your daily routine?

Well, um... I feel like we're kind of circling back to this, and I really don't want to sound like my life is falling apart or anything. It's really not! I'm still keeping up with my daily routine overall. I get up, I go to work, I run my company... I'm doing all the things I'm supposed to do.

It's just... like I mentioned earlier, I guess the interference is more about the relationships than the routine itself? Like, I'm doing the routine, but when I get sidetracked, it's costing me that trust at home with my wife when our family plans get messed up. And at work, it's losing the patience of my team when meetings or mentoring conversations go off track. 

So, it's not that I can't function or get through my day, I promise. It's just... the way things don't always go the way they should is starting to affect the people around me, and I really hate that. I'm trying so hard to fix it, though. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I just want to make sure you know I'm still handling things as best I can.
Are you finding that your difficulties with staying on track are causing problems in your relationships with friends, beyond just your family and work team?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, my friends and I... we're all pretty busy, you know? So if I'm a little scattered when we do catch up, they don't really seem to mind. I'm still the same guy they've always known. 

I really try to make sure I'm present when I'm with them. We mostly just grab a drink or watch a game, so there isn't a lot of pressure to be super organized anyway. I definitely wouldn't say I'm causing any problems with my friends. I think I'm doing okay there... at least, I hope I am? I'd hate to think I was letting them down, too. But no, I haven't noticed any issues with my buddies.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus or making careless mistakes, since childhood?

Well, um... I really wouldn't say I had a big problem with focus or making mistakes back then. I mean, I didn't finish high school, but that was more about wanting to get out there and start working, not because I couldn't pay attention. I was always a really hard worker, even as a kid!

But, I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, there were some things. It wasn't about being careless, I promise! It was just... I had a lot of energy. Looking back, I remember teachers were always having to move my seat. They said I talked a bit too much, or I'd just get up without asking because I felt like I needed to move. And sometimes I'd just blurt out an answer before they even finished asking the question... I just got so excited to participate, you know? 

I wasn't trying to be disruptive or bad, I swear. I just had a hard time sitting still and keeping quiet. But I always tried my best to be a good kid. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker... I really wasn't!
Have you always had difficulty sustaining focus or paying attention for as long as you can remember?

Well, um... I wouldn't say *always*, and I really don't want to make it sound like I can't pay attention at all. I really do try my best to stay focused, especially when it's important! 

But, I guess... well, sometimes at work, I can start reading a planning document, or I'll sit down with one of my managers, and I promise, for the first few minutes, I am completely locked in. I'm totally engaged. But then... I don't know, pretty soon I'll sort of realize I just missed half of what was said, or my eyes just glazed over the page. And I have to ask them to, you know, run it back or repeat themselves. 

I always apologize when I have to ask them to do that. I really don't want them to think I don't care about what they're saying, because I do! I value their input so much. It's just a little blip, really. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad boss or anything... I just drift a little sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a child?

Well, um, we kind of just touched on that, right? I mean, I really don't want to keep harping on it and sound like I was a bad kid, because I promise I wasn't! I always wanted to do the right thing. 

But yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago, looking back... teachers were always having to move my seat around. It wasn't because I was being mean or anything, I just... I guess I talked a bit too much. And I'd get out of my chair without asking, or I'd just blurt out the answer before the teacher even finished their sentence. I just wanted to be involved, you know? I was just really eager. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was totally out of control back then. I really tried my best to be good! Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much.
Did you have significant difficulty paying attention or following instructions as a child?

Well, um... I feel like we're sort of covering the same ground here, aren't we? I really don't mean to sound defensive, I promise! I just... I don't want to give you the wrong impression about how I was as a kid. 

Like I said, I didn't really have a big problem with focus. I mean, I didn't finish high school, but that wasn't because I couldn't follow instructions or pay attention. I just wanted to get out into the world and start working! I was always a hard worker, even back then. I always tried to do what I was told and be helpful. 

I really don't think I had significant difficulty with that stuff. I mean, maybe a little bit, like any kid, but nothing major. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right without making myself sound like I was a problem child. I really wasn't! Does that help clear things up?
Did you often have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you were in elementary school?

Oh, um... specifically elementary school? Gosh, I hope I'm not frustrating you, I feel like I keep giving you the same answer and I really don't want to be difficult! 

But honestly... no, I don't remember having trouble with instructions back in the early grades either. I mean, like I said, I was definitely a bit chatty and eager to jump out of my seat, but when the teacher actually gave us instructions, I really tried my absolute hardest to follow them. I always wanted to be the teacher's helper, you know? I hated the idea of getting in trouble or disappointing them. 

So I don't think paying attention to the rules or following along was a problem for me back then. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you what you're looking for! Does that answer it?
Did you have any symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty paying attention or following instructions, when you were a teenager?

Um, as a teenager? Gosh, I feel terrible because I feel like I'm just giving you the exact same answer again. I really hope you don't think I'm being evasive or anything! 

But no, even in high school, I didn't really have trouble paying attention or following instructions. I know I left school early to start working—which I know probably sounds bad on paper, and I really don't want you to think I was some rebellious teen who wouldn't listen to authority! I just... I had all this drive and wanted to get out there and be productive, you know? Start building something. 

But when I was actually there, in the classroom, I paid attention just fine. I could follow along and I always tried to be respectful of the teachers. I just didn't have that specific problem. I hope that's okay? I'm really trying my best to give you good answers here, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
